{"parentUuid":"1a06914e-ff24-4dcb-8bb7-7367b226ad40","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"mcp_instructions_delta","addedNames":["plugin:context7:context7","plugin:serena:serena"],"addedBlocks":["## plugin:context7:context7\nUse this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service -- even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer -- your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.\n\nDo not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.","## plugin:serena:serena\nCRITICAL: Before starting to work on a coding task, call the `initial_instructions` tool to read the 'Serena Instructions Manual'."],"removedNames":[]},"type":"attachment","uuid":"95579d61-cbe6-4ca2-a919-947820d42602","timestamp":"2026-05-14T10:53:55.281Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"efc2e2f4-4622-42c4-be6b-a34fbc9cd3d4","version":"2.1.138","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"95579d61-cbe6-4ca2-a919-947820d42602","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- empirical-probe-first: Probe ALL viable strategies in a multi-option ladder BEFORE committing to one. Use when a session-plan / decision-ADR / spec presents ≥3 strategy options (e.g. \"Strategy A1/A2/A3\" or \"alternative B/C/D\") and the recommended option's source-evidence may be stale. Outputs a probe matrix per strategy + commit decision with empirical citation. Pairs with `vendor-api-probe.sh` (deterministic detection layer; SessionStart hook) and `decompose-work` (deterministic-vs-LLM split per probe). Charter promotion target — codifies L-S32-1 doctrine surfaced at S32 Track A pivot (master-plan recommended A2 vnstock alternate; empirical probe rejected A1+A2; A3 SSI direct httpx adopted instead).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use during sandwich-verifier review, drift investigation, or post-mortem when component-telemetry.jsonl + dispatch.jsonl + sessions-rollup.tsv need cross-checking.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- sync-pull: On-demand confidence-score lookup before a SCOPE+/ARCH/IMPL decision. Reads agent-workspace/memory/sync-tracker/state.tsv + weights.yaml; surfaces the relevant category's score, tier, must-grill flag, and the decision-class threshold. {"parentUuid":"4fb61a2f-4255-4c36-b871-5aa8105ee230","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"b7e2b130-644e-4954-8f6f-8dff74ec61b0","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01QD4AJFdiciZA6FwepTRi4b","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# PROJECT CHARTER\n2\t## StockForge — Personal Investment Advisor for Vietnamese Stock Market\n3\t\n4\t> **Status**: Immutable v1.1 — changes require explicit charter revision.\n5\t> **Revision history**: v1.0 → v1.1 (2026-05-12, D-056): Added Principle 11 — Harness must self-verify firing, not self-attest existence.\n6\t> **Scope of immutability**: Vision, principles, success criteria.\n7\t> **Things that do evolve**: Agent configs, specs, implementation, signal weights, eval sets.\n8\t\n9\t---\n10\t\n11\t## Vision\n12\t\n13\tAn AI-first investment research and advisory system that combines **quant fund methodology** with **Vietnam-specific edge sources** (KOL networks, crowd sentiment, pump pattern detection) to surface high-conviction opportunities in an inefficient market where logic-based screening alone is insufficient.\n14\t\n15\tPrimary user: project owner (self) + 3-5 trusted peers in Vietnamese investing community.\n16\t\n17\tPrimary goal: build a system that compounds edge over time through proprietary data accumulation, not through any single clever algorithm. After 12-24 months of dogfood, the system should be a genuine advisor I would pay money for if someone else built it.\n18\t\n19\tNot a goal: high-frequency trading, replacing human judgment, becoming a SaaS in Year 1, beating frontier LLMs at general reasoning, providing licensed financial advice.\n20\t\n21\t---\n22\t\n23\t## The Core Insight (the why)\n24\t\n25\t**Quant funds (Renaissance, Two Sigma, DE Shaw) win in efficient markets through clean data + execution speed + diverse alpha factors.** They don't use sentiment from Facebook/YouTube because at their scale it's noise, not signal — and in efficient markets it gets arbitraged away anyway.\n26\t\n27\t**Vietnam stock market inverts this.** It is structurally inefficient:\n28\t- 85-90% retail investor share (vs 20-25% in US)\n29\t- Information asymmetry between sophisticated and retail crowd\n30\t- KOL/influencer recommendations measurably move prices\n31\t- \"Đội lái\" (pump operators) operate openly\n32\t- News and narrative cycles dominate over fundamentals for months at a time\n33\t- Foreign flow creates non-fundamental price pressure\n34\t\n35\tIn this market, **sentiment + influence + narrative tracking is signal, not noise**. And LLMs can process Vietnamese unstructured text at scale that was impossible before 2023.\n36\t\n37\tThis creates a **structural arbitrage**: apply quant methodology + LLM reasoning + sentiment/influence data layers that no commercial product offers for VN. Position not as \"decision maker\" but as **advisor + alert watcher + bias mirror**.\n38\t\n39\t---\n40\t\n41\t## The Craft Philosophy\n42\t\n43\tTake the craft seriously. Build for personal use first, commercial second.\n44\t\n45\t- Production-grade engineering standards from Day 1 (DDD + clean architecture + multi-loop discipline)\n46\t- Commercial extension kept as option, never as driver\n47\t- When self-use conflicts with hypothetical-future-SaaS, self-use wins\n48\t- Quality bar: I genuinely trust output enough to act on real money decisions\n49\t- Edge comes from compounding moats (proprietary data, calibration, personal bias log), not from any single feature\n50\t\n51\tReference models: Renaissance Technologies (data + iteration discipline), Bridgewater (principles-based decision making), personal Bloomberg Terminal (data density + analysis depth), Athletic.com (subscription-quality content for niche audience).\n52\t\n53\t---\n54\t\n55\t## Core Principles (non-negotiable)\n56\t\n57\t1. **Evidence grounding** — every claim, every number traceable to source + as-of date. Hallucination in finance = bug, not stylistic issue.\n58\t\n59\t2. **Structured output over narrative** — multi-criteria assessment, never single \"buy/sell\" score. Output is trade-off matrix.\n60\t\n61\t3. **Adversarial by design** — bear + bull + critic + quant + behavior + manager perspectives. Never consensus from single agent.\n62\t\n63\t4. **Proprietary data moat** — every news ingested, every KOL recommendation tracked, every thesis post-mortem'd compounds the edge. Raw data is sacred.\n64\t\n65\t5. **Pattern transfer + local adaptation** — global setups (cyclical bottom, dividend value, GARP) + Vietnam-specific overlays (policy timing, foreign flow, narrative phase).\n66\t\n67\t6. **Human-in-loop is the product** — augment thinking, never replace it. System should challenge user's gut instinct without overriding it.\n68\t\n69\t7. **Dogfood mandatory** — if I don't use it weekly for real decisions, the feature gets killed. Self-use is the only validation that matters in Year 1.\n70\t\n71\t8. **Calibration over confidence** — system tracks its own accuracy across signal types, never claims confidence it hasn't earned through hit rate.\n72\t\n73\t9. **No LLM math** — LLM never generates numbers. All calculations through deterministic code with verified data inputs. LLM only interprets.\n74\t\n75\t10. **Position sizing & risk management are deterministic** — code-enforced rules, LLM cannot override. Maximum position size, sector concentration, stop loss rules are immutable per session.\n76\t\n77\t11. **Harness must self-verify firing, not self-attest existence** — Every hook ships with a companion firing-test in `scripts/hooks/firing-tests/`; the continuous `harness-health-self-scan` hook verifies signal-set HH-1 through HH-N (codified in `agent-workspace/constitution/harness-health-protocol.md`) on every UserPromptSubmit + SessionStart event. Ritual closure of a track (file existence + smoke-test exit 0) is forbidden until empirical-firing evidence (production log entry / artifact / telemetry row from real session activity) is captured.\n78\t\n79\t---\n80\t\n81\t## The Four-Tier Signal Architecture\n82\t\n83\tSystem operates on four distinct signal tiers, each with different lead time, reliability, and processing approach:\n84\t\n85\t**Tier 1 — Hard Data (deterministic):** prices, volumes, fundamentals, foreign flow, macro indicators. Zero LLM, pure code. Lead time: hours-days.\n86\t\n87\t**Tier 2 — Official Narrative (semi-structured):** mainstream financial news, broker reports, official company disclosures, government announcements. LLM extracts claims + classifies sentiment + detects contradictions. Lead time: real-time.\n88\t\n89\t**Tier 3 — Influence Network (semi-structured):** YouTube channels, Facebook KOL pages, Telegram channels, podcasts. LLM transcribes + extracts recommendations + tags entities. Calibration database tracks each KOL's accuracy over time. Lead time: can lead by days.\n90\t\n91\t**Tier 4 — Crowd Sentiment & Pump Detection (unstructured):** community forums, public chat groups, comments. LLM classifies sentiment + detects coordinated posting + identifies pump narratives + tracks narrative lifecycle phase. Lead time: typically lags price (signals exhaustion).\n92\t\n93\tThe combination — when Tier 1+2+3 agree before Tier 4 heats up = early opportunity; when Tier 4 hot but Tier 1+2 don't support = likely top — is the core analytical edge.\n94\t\n95\tSee `specs/tier1-strategic/001-four-tier-signal-architecture.md` for detailed tier specs.\n96\t\n97\t---\n98\t\n99\t## First Sub-Scope (locked 6 months)\n100\t\n101\t**Vietnam stocks listed on HOSE/HNX/UPCoM**, specifically:\n102\t- VN30 + mid-cap (vốn hóa 2,000-50,000 tỷ VND) for primary coverage\n103\t- Long-only equity strategies (no derivatives, no shorting)\n104\t- Holding periods: 1-month minimum, 6-24 month preferred\n105\t- Position sizing per stock: 5-15% of portfolio\n106\t\n107\tOut of scope (Year 1): derivatives, warrants (CW), short selling, cryptocurrency, fund products, foreign markets, day trading, automated execution.\n108\t\n109\t---\n110\t\n111\t## Honest Boundaries (what system does NOT do)\n112\t\n113\t- **Predict price** — system predicts narrative phase, money flow direction, mispricing level. Never a price target with false precision.\n114\t- **Replace fundamental research** — surfaces opportunities, user must verify thesis before acting.\n115\t- **Execute trades** — pure research/alert tool. Execution stays manual.\n116\t- **Provide licensed financial advice** — personal research aid only. Output explicitly framed as \"thesis exploration\", not \"buy/sell recommendation\".\n117\t- **Time the market precisely** — works on phase identification (early/mid/late), not on tick-level timing.\n118\t- **Insider information** — uses only public sources. No paid leaks, no insider channels, no anything that crosses legal/ethical lines.\n119\t\n120\t---\n121\t\n122\t## Success Criteria\n123\t\n124\t**Month 3 (end of Phase 1 — Foundation):**\n125\t- Tier 1 + 2 data pipeline operational for VN30\n126\t- 50 companies have basic dossier in wiki\n127\t- First 5 thesis recorded with formal structure\n128\t- Can run /thesis-validate on a stock end-to-end in <5 minutes\n129\t\n130\t**Month 6 (end of Phase 2 — Edge Sources):**\n131\t- 30+ KOL channels tracked, calibration database has >100 recommendations with outcomes pending\n132\t- Tier 3 + 4 ingestion operational for top 100 stocks\n133\t- First detectable pump pattern caught (warning issued before public dump)\n134\t- 20+ thesis logged, first 5 hit 3-month review\n135\t\n136\t**Month 9 (end of Phase 3 — Multi-perspective):**\n137\t- Bear/bull/critic/quant/macro/behavior agents operational\n138\t- Pattern library has 15+ Vietnam-specific patterns with outcome data\n139\t- Personal bias log shows 3+ identified biases\n140\t- Thesis hit rate measurable (statistically meaningful sample)\n141\t\n142\t**Month 12 (end of Phase 4 — Compounding):**\n143\t- Karpathy outer loop optimizing signal weights weekly\n144\t- Cross-validation: system suggestions vs my manual analysis = where do they diverge?\n145\t- 3-5 trusted peers using it, providing feedback\n146\t- Demonstrable alpha vs VN-Index on dogfood portfolio (or honest accounting of why not)\n147\t\n148\t**Ultimate signal of success**: When my gut says \"buy XYZ\", I check what StockForge says first — and seriously consider it when it disagrees.\n149\t\n150\t---\n151\t\n152\t## Technical Foundation (locked Phase 1-3)\n153\t\n154\t**Stack:**\n155\t- **Python primary** — for data science, LLM workflows, time-series, backtesting (heavier than IdeaForge which was TS-primary)\n156\t- **Postgres 16 + TimescaleDB + pgvector + pg_trgm** — single DB for time-series + relational + vector\n157\t- **Redis** — cache + pub/sub + queue broker\n158\t- **Cloudflare R2** — raw content storage (PDFs, transcripts, scraped pages)\n159\t- **Claude API primary** — Sonnet for most tasks, Opus for thesis synthesis\n160\t- **OpenAI embeddings** — text-embedding-3-small (Vietnamese acceptable)\n161\t- **NestJS** — only if/when we need a public-facing API (Phase 4+)\n162\t- **Streamlit/Next.js** — Streamlit for personal dashboard (Phase 1-2), Next.js if SaaS path\n163\t- **Apache Airflow / Prefect** — data pipeline orchestration\n164\t\n165\t**Architecture:**\n166\t- Clean Architecture with DDD tactical patterns (same as IdeaForge)\n167\t- 9 bounded contexts (see `agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md`)\n168\t- Event-driven for cross-context communication\n169\t- Multi-loop execution (Karpathy outer + Continuous middle + Per-stock inner)\n170\t\n171\t**Development approach:**\n172\t- AI-first: Claude Code as primary builder, human as spec author + reviewer + bias-checker\n173\t- Spec-Driven (SDD) + Domain-Driven (DDD) + selective BDD\n174\t- Sandwich pattern (Architect → Dev → Verifier) from Day 1\n175\t- Verify-Before-Write (VBW) protocol mandatory\n176\t- Three-tier quality gates (deterministic / probabilistic / human)\n177\t\n178\t---\n179\t\n180\t## Data Sources (Tier 1 budget)\n181\t\n182\t**Free/cheap (Phase 1):**\n183\t- vnstock (open source) — historical EOD, fundamentals\n184\t- Vietstock public — financial reports\n185\t- TCBS API — semi-public market data\n186\t- CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz — news scraping\n187\t- Public YouTube channels — transcript via yt-dlp + Whisper\n188\t- Public Facebook fanpages — selective scraping (legal grey, careful scope)\n189\t\n190\t**Paid (Phase 2-3 if budget allows):**\n191\t- FiinPro Platform — comprehensive fundamental data (~30-100M VND/year)\n192\t- Wichart — pre-cleaned data\n193\t- SSI FastConnect — realtime quotes if needed\n194\t\n195\t**Budget cap Year 1**: 50M VND for data + LLM combined.\n196\t\n197\t---\n198\t\n199\t## Meta-Discipline\n200\t\n201\tThese charter principles override daily decisions:\n202\t\n203\t- **When in doubt, simplify** — minimum code that solves the problem, nothing speculative\n204\t- **Ship thin slices, not perfect systems** — each phase ends with something I actually use\n205\t- **Document what you learn, not what you plan** — post-mortem > prospective docs\n206\t- **Dogfood or delete** — features I don't use weekly get removed\n207\t- **Calibrate, don't guess** — every confidence claim must have outcome tracking\n208\t- **Stay agnostic about commercial outcome** — build for the craft, not for the exit\n209\t\n210\t---\n211\t\n212\t## Revision Protocol\n213\t\n214\tThis charter changes only when:\n215\t- A core principle proves materially wrong through 30+ hours of real use\n216\t- Scope demonstrably needs revision based on accumulated dogfood data\n217\t- Technical foundation invalidated by external event (tool deprecation, regulatory change, etc.)\n218\t\n219\tCharter revisions require:\n220\t- Written rationale with evidence (linked to specific sessions/post-mortems)\n221\t- 48-hour cool-down before committing change\n222\t- Explicit version bump (v1.0 → v2.0)\n223\t\n224\tMinor clarifications go in `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md`. This charter stays stable.\n225\t\n226\t---\n227\t\n228\t## Document Index\n229\t\n230\t| Document | Purpose | Stability |\n231\t|---|---|---|\n232\t| `PROJECT_CHARTER.md` (this) | Vision + principles | Immutable for ~3 months |\n233\t| `AGENT_OPERATING_MANUAL.md` | Agent configs, skills, workflows | Living, frequent updates |\n234\t| `SPEC_TEMPLATE.md` | How to write specs | Stable |\n235\t| `specs/tier1-strategic/001-four-tier-signal-architecture.md` | Strategic: signal architecture | Stable |\n236\t| `specs/tier2-feature/001-validate-investment-thesis.md` | First implementation spec | Stable |\n237\t| `specs/tier2-feature/002-influence-network-tracking.md` | KOL tracking system spec | Stable |\n238\t| `specs/tier2-feature/003-crowd-sentiment-pump-detection.md` | Pump detection spec | Stable |\n239\t| `specs/tier2-feature/004-multi-perspective-adversarial-agents.md` | Adversarial analysis spec | Stable |\n240\t| `specs/tier2-feature/005-karpathy-outer-loop.md` | Pipeline self-optimization spec | Stable |\n241\t| `agent-workspace/memory/project.md` | Current state | Continuously updated |\n242\t| `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` | Learned rules | Append-mostly |\n243\t| `agent-workspace/memory/thesis-log/` | All thesis ever recorded | Append-only |\n244\t| `agent-workspace/memory/post-mortems/` | Thesis outcome reviews | Append-only |\n245\t| `agent-workspace/calibration/` | KOL accuracy, signal calibration data | Continuously updated |\n246\t\n247\t---\n248\t\n249\t## Anti-Charter (what we explicitly reject)\n250\t\n251\tTo stay focused, we reject these tempting paths:\n252\t\n253\t- **Predict prices with ML models** — models trained on VN price data overfit; no edge there.\n254\t- **Compete with broker research** — we have less data, less staff. We win on integration + edge sources, not on raw analysis depth.\n255\t- **Build for general retail public** — we build for ourselves and 3-5 peers. Mass market needs hand-holding we won't provide.\n256\t- **Trust LLM for numbers** — every numerical output must come from code with traceable inputs.\n257\t- **Build features without dogfooding** — speculative features die fast in this project.\n258\t- **Optimize for backtest performance** — Goodhart's Law is real. We optimize for forward decision quality.\n259\t- **Make money fast** — this is a 24-month project minimum to reach edge. Quick wins are anti-pattern.\n260\t"}]},"uuid":"34c7fc17-81df-42ce-91bf-bfa19720e6b8","timestamp":"2026-05-14T10:54:10.696Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\PROJECT_CHARTER.md","content":"# PROJECT CHARTER\n## StockForge — Personal Investment Advisor for Vietnamese Stock Market\n\n> **Status**: Immutable v1.1 — changes require explicit charter revision.\n> **Revision history**: v1.0 → v1.1 (2026-05-12, D-056): Added Principle 11 — Harness must self-verify firing, not self-attest existence.\n> **Scope of immutability**: Vision, principles, success criteria.\n> **Things that do evolve**: Agent configs, specs, implementation, signal weights, eval sets.\n\n---\n\n## Vision\n\nAn AI-first investment research and advisory system that combines **quant fund methodology** with **Vietnam-specific edge sources** (KOL networks, crowd sentiment, pump pattern detection) to surface high-conviction opportunities in an inefficient market where logic-based screening alone is insufficient.\n\nPrimary user: project owner (self) + 3-5 trusted peers in Vietnamese investing community.\n\nPrimary goal: build a system that compounds edge over time through proprietary data accumulation, not through any single clever algorithm. Hallucination in finance = bug, not stylistic issue.\n\n2. **Structured output over narrative** — multi-criteria assessment, never single \"buy/sell\" score. Output is trade-off matrix.\n\n3. **Adversarial by design** — bear + bull + critic + quant + behavior + manager perspectives. Never consensus from single agent.\n\n4. **Proprietary data moat** — every news ingested, every KOL recommendation tracked, every thesis post-mortem'd compounds the edge. Raw data is sacred.\n\n5. **Pattern transfer + local adaptation** — global setups (cyclical bottom, dividend value, GARP) + Vietnam-specific overlays (policy timing, foreign flow, narrative phase).\n\n6. **Human-in-loop is the product** — augment thinking, never replace it. System should challenge user's gut instinct without overriding it.\n\n7. **Dogfood mandatory** — if I don't use it weekly for real decisions, the feature gets killed. Self-use is the only validation that matters in Year 1.\n\n8. **Calibration over confidence** — system tracks its own accuracy across signal types, never claims confidence it hasn't earned through hit rate.\n\n9. **No LLM math** — LLM never generates numbers. All calculations through deterministic code with verified data inputs. LLM only interprets.\n\n10. **Position sizing & risk management are deterministic** — code-enforced rules, LLM cannot override. Maximum position size, sector concentration, stop loss rules are immutable per session.\n\n11. **Harness must self-verify firing, not self-attest existence** — Every hook ships with a companion firing-test in `scripts/hooks/firing-tests/`; the continuous `harness-health-self-scan` hook verifies signal-set HH-1 through HH-N (codified in `agent-workspace/constitution/harness-health-protocol.md`) on every UserPromptSubmit + SessionStart event. Ritual closure of a track (file existence + smoke-test exit 0) is forbidden until empirical-firing evidence (production log entry / artifact / telemetry row from real session activity) is captured.\n\n---\n\n## The Four-Tier Signal Architecture\n\nSystem operates on four distinct signal tiers, each with different lead time, reliability, and processing approach:\n\n**Tier 1 — Hard Data (deterministic):** prices, volumes, fundamentals, foreign flow, macro indicators. Zero LLM, pure code. Lead time: hours-days.\n\n**Tier 2 — Official Narrative (semi-structured):** mainstream financial news, broker reports, official company disclosures, government announcements. LLM extracts claims + classifies sentiment + detects contradictions. Lead time: real-time.\n\n**Tier 3 — Influence Network (semi-structured):** YouTube channels, Facebook KOL pages, Telegram channels, podcasts. LLM transcribes + extracts recommendations + tags entities. Calibration database tracks each KOL's accuracy over time. Lead time: can lead by days.\n\n**Tier 4 — Crowd Sentiment & Pump Detection (unstructured):** community forums, public chat groups, comments. LLM classifies sentiment + detects coordinated posting + identifies pump narratives + tracks narrative lifecycle phase. Lead time: typically lags price (signals exhaustion).\n\nThe combination — when Tier 1+2+3 agree before Tier 4 heats up = early opportunity; when Tier 4 hot but Tier 1+2 don't support = likely top — is the core analytical edge.\n\nSee `specs/tier1-strategic/001-four-tier-signal-architecture.md` for detailed tier specs.\n\n---\n\n## First Sub-Scope (locked 6 months)\n\n**Vietnam stocks listed on HOSE/HNX/UPCoM**, specifically:\n- VN30 + mid-cap (vốn hóa 2,000-50,000 tỷ VND) for primary coverage\n- Long-only equity strategies (no derivatives, no shorting)\n- Holding periods: 1-month minimum, 6-24 month preferred\n- Position sizing per stock: 5-15% of portfolio\n\nOut of scope (Year 1): derivatives, warrants (CW), short selling, cryptocurrency, fund products, foreign markets, day trading, automated execution.\n\n---\n\n## Honest Boundaries (what system does NOT do)\n\n- **Predict price** — system predicts narrative phase, money flow direction, mispricing level. Never a price target with false precision.\n- **Replace fundamental research** — surfaces opportunities, user must verify thesis before acting.\n- **Execute trades** — pure research/alert tool. Execution stays manual.\n- **Provide licensed financial advice** — personal research aid only. Output explicitly framed as \"thesis exploration\", not \"buy/sell recommendation\".\n- **Time the market precisely** — works on phase identification (early/mid/late), not on tick-level timing.\n- **Insider information** — uses only public sources. No paid leaks, no insider channels, no anything that crosses legal/ethical lines.\n\n---\n\n## Success Criteria\n\n**Month 3 (end of Phase 1 — Foundation):**\n- Tier 1 + 2 data pipeline operational for VN30\n- 50 companies have basic dossier in wiki\n- First 5 thesis recorded with formal structure\n- Can run /thesis-validate on a stock end-to-end in <5 minutes\n\n**Month 6 (end of Phase 2 — Edge Sources):**\n- 30+ KOL channels tracked, calibration database has >100 recommendations with outcomes pending\n- Tier 3 + 4 ingestion operational for top 100 stocks\n- First detectable pump pattern caught (warning issued before public dump)\n- 20+ thesis logged, first 5 hit 3-month review\n\n**Month 9 (end of Phase 3 — Multi-perspective):**\n- Bear/bull/critic/quant/macro/behavior agents operational\n- Pattern library has 15+ Vietnam-specific patterns with outcome data\n- Personal bias log shows 3+ identified biases\n- Thesis hit rate measurable (statistically meaningful sample)\n\n**Month 12 (end of Phase 4 — Compounding):**\n- Karpathy outer loop optimizing signal weights weekly\n- Cross-validation: system suggestions vs my manual analysis = where do they diverge?\n- 3-5 trusted peers using it, providing feedback\n- Demonstrable alpha vs VN-Index on dogfood portfolio (or honest accounting of why not)\n\n**Ultimate signal of success**: When my gut says \"buy XYZ\", I check what StockForge says first — and seriously consider it when it disagrees.\n\n---\n\n## Technical Foundation (locked Phase 1-3)\n\n**Stack:**\n- **Python primary** — for data science, LLM workflows, time-series, backtesting (heavier than IdeaForge which was TS-primary)\n- **Postgres 16 + TimescaleDB + pgvector + pg_trgm** — single DB for time-series + relational + vector\n- **Redis** — cache + pub/sub + queue broker\n- **Cloudflare R2** — raw content storage (PDFs, transcripts, scraped pages)\n- **Claude API primary** — Sonnet for most tasks, Opus for thesis synthesis\n- **OpenAI embeddings** — text-embedding-3-small (Vietnamese acceptable)\n- **NestJS** — only if/when we need a public-facing API (Phase 4+)\n- **Streamlit/Next.js** — Streamlit for personal dashboard (Phase 1-2), Next.js if SaaS path\n- **Apache Airflow / Prefect** — data pipeline orchestration\n\n**Architecture:**\n- Clean Architecture with DDD tactical patterns (same as IdeaForge)\n- 9 bounded contexts (see `agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md`)\n- Event-driven for cross-context communication\n- Multi-loop execution (Karpathy outer + Continuous middle + Per-stock inner)\n\n**Development approach:**\n- AI-first: Claude Code as primary builder, human as spec author + reviewer + bias-checker\n- Spec-Driven (SDD) + Domain-Driven (DDD) + selective BDD\n- Sandwich pattern (Architect → Dev → Verifier) from Day 1\n- Verify-Before-Write (VBW) protocol mandatory\n- Three-tier quality gates (deterministic / probabilistic / human)\n\n---\n\n## Data Sources (Tier 1 budget)\n\n**Free/cheap (Phase 1):**\n- vnstock (open source) — historical EOD, fundamentals\n- Vietstock public — financial reports\n- TCBS API — semi-public market data\n- CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz — news scraping\n- Public YouTube channels — transcript via yt-dlp + Whisper\n- Public Facebook fanpages — selective scraping (legal grey, careful scope)\n\n**Paid (Phase 2-3 if budget allows):**\n- FiinPro Platform — comprehensive fundamental data (~30-100M VND/year)\n- Wichart — pre-cleaned data\n- SSI FastConnect — realtime quotes if needed\n\n**Budget cap Year 1**: 50M VND for data + LLM combined.\n\n---\n\n## Meta-Discipline\n\nThese charter principles override daily decisions:\n\n- **When in doubt, simplify** — minimum code that solves the problem, nothing speculative\n- **Ship thin slices, not perfect systems** — each phase ends with something I actually use\n- **Document what you learn, not what you plan** — post-mortem > prospective docs\n- **Dogfood or delete** — features I don't use weekly get removed\n- **Calibrate, don't guess** — every confidence claim must have outcome tracking\n- **Stay agnostic about commercial outcome** — build for the craft, not for the exit\n\n---\n\n## Revision Protocol\n\nThis charter changes only when:\n- A core principle proves materially wrong through 30+ hours of real use\n- Scope demonstrably needs revision based on accumulated dogfood data\n- Technical foundation invalidated by external event (tool deprecation, regulatory change, etc.)\n\nCharter revisions require:\n- Written rationale with evidence (linked to specific sessions/post-mortems)\n- 48-hour cool-down before committing change\n- Explicit version bump (v1.0 → v2.0)\n\nMinor clarifications go in `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md`. This charter stays stable.\n\n---\n\n## Document Index\n\n| Document | Purpose | Stability |\n|---|---|---|\n| `PROJECT_CHARTER.md` (this) | Vision + principles | Immutable for ~3 months |\n| `AGENT_OPERATING_MANUAL.md` | Agent configs, skills, workflows | Living, frequent updates |\n| `SPEC_TEMPLATE.md` | How to write specs | Stable |\n| `specs/tier1-strategic/001-four-tier-signal-architecture.md` | Strategic: signal architecture | Stable |\n| `specs/tier2-feature/001-validate-investment-thesis.md` | First implementation spec | Stable |\n| `specs/tier2-feature/002-influence-network-tracking.md` | KOL tracking system spec | Stable |\n| `specs/tier2-feature/003-crowd-sentiment-pump-detection.md` | Pump detection spec | Stable |\n| `specs/tier2-feature/004-multi-perspective-adversarial-agents.md` | Adversarial analysis spec | Stable |\n| `specs/tier2-feature/005-karpathy-outer-loop.md` | Pipeline self-optimization spec | Stable |\n| `agent-workspace/memory/project.md` | Current state | Continuously updated |\n| `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` | Learned rules | Append-mostly |\n| `agent-workspace/memory/thesis-log/` | All thesis ever recorded | Append-only |\n| `agent-workspace/memory/post-mortems/` | Thesis outcome reviews | Append-only |\n| `agent-workspace/calibration/` | KOL accuracy, signal calibration data | Continuously updated |\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Charter (what we explicitly reject)\n\nTo stay focused, we reject these tempting paths:\n\n- **Predict prices with ML models** — models trained on VN price data overfit; no edge there.\n- **Compete with broker research** — we have less data, less staff. We win on integration + edge sources, not on raw analysis depth.\n- **Build for general retail public** — we build for ourselves and 3-5 peers. Mass market needs hand-holding we won't provide.\n- **Trust LLM for numbers** — every numerical output must come from code with traceable inputs.\n- **Build features without dogfooding** — speculative features die fast in this project.\n- **Optimize for backtest performance** — Goodhart's Law is real. We optimize for forward decision quality.\n- **Make money fast** — this is a 24-month project minimum to reach edge. Quick wins are anti-pattern.\n","numLines":260,"startLine":1,"totalLines":260}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"4fb61a2f-4255-4c36-b871-5aa8105ee230","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"efc2e2f4-4622-42c4-be6b-a34fbc9cd3d4","version":"2.1.138","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"34c7fc17-81df-42ce-91bf-bfa19720e6b8","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"nested_memory","path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\CLAUDE.md","content":{"path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\CLAUDE.md","type":"Project","content":"# agent-workspace/ — Contract\r\n\r\n> **Audience**: agents working inside `agent-workspace/`.\r\n> **Established**: Decision 002 § Track 1 (Workspace Dualism Foundation).\r\n\r\n## Identity\r\n\r\n`agent-workspace/` is the **agent-owned execution + memory** layer. Everything here represents **agent state, decisions, plans, observations, learning**. Agents WRITE here freely (within constitution rules); humans READ here but normally do not edit.\r\n\r\nThis separation exists to prevent two failure modes from orch:\r\n1. **Charter drift via shared-workspace mutation** (orch CF-DOGFOOD-2)\r\n2. **Human cognitive overload from dense session logs** (UP02 §1.3 — \"human đối mặt hàng chục spec/document quá tải nếu không sắp xếp khoa học\")\r\n\r\nThe agent owns this directory but must keep it AUDITABLE — every artifact provenance-linked, every decision sourced.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Subdirectories\r\n\r\n| Path | Purpose | Lifecycle |\r\n|---|---|---|\r\n| `constitution/` | **IMMUTABLE without explicit user approval**. Charter-tier rules (autonomous-protocol, model-routing, identity-scope, etc.). Track 7 produces drafts in `proposals/`; user explicit approve to move here. | Edit denied by .claude/settings.json; Write only via human approval gate |\r\n| `memory/project.md` | High-level project state; phase tracker; ADRs (last 5). Update on phase boundaries + architectural decisions. | Long-lived; trim to most recent decisions |\r\n| `memory/current-execution.md` | **THE single routing source of truth**. Read FIRST every session. | Long-lived; updated each session boundary |\r\n| `memory/agent-notes.md` | Learned rules from real experience (post-mortem / drift / user correction). Append-only mostly. | Long-lived |\r\n| `memory/decisions/` | Sequential ADRs (`NNN-<slug>.md`) + `_template.md` + `README.md` index. 12-field schema (Track 2). | Append-only; supersession via status field |\r\n| `memory/sessions/` | One file per session: `YYYY-MM-DD-session-N.md`. What happened, decisions made, files touched. | Append-only |\r\n| `memory/observations/` | Subagent return artifacts (per Track 6 spec). Each subagent writes one observation file describing what it did. | Append; cleaned periodically by aggregator |\r\n| `memory/checkpoints/` | Session handoff state for self-reboot (Track 5). `latest.md` is canonical pointer; timestamped historical files retained. | Append + latest.md updated each checkpoint |\r\n| `memory/patterns-discovered/` | Pattern mining outputs (Track 0 — DONE) + ongoing pattern catalog. | Append; significant patterns promoted to constitution |\r\n| `memory/drift-logs/` | Drift-check (DR1-DR12) results; runs on hook + on-demand. | Time-series append |\r\n| `memory/post-mortems/` | After significant failure or thesis-revoked event: what failed, root cause, prevention rule. | Append |\r\n| `memory/thesis-log/` | Stock-domain thesis exploration entries. Read-only for IMPL sessions. | Append + revisited per calibration |\r\n| `memory/sync-tracker/` | Track 8a output: Confidence Score SQLite + weights.yaml + auto-rendered `_index.md`. | Live updated by hooks |\r\n| `memory/self-awareness/` | Track 9 output: model × effort × thinking profile cards + known-issues + best-practices. | Live updated by Stop-hook aggregator |\r\n| `memory/mistake-log.md` | Track 7 deliverable: structured failure catalog. What went wrong / Root cause / Prevention rule / Severity. | Append; pre-flight read by all agents |\r\n| `session-plans/pending/` | Plans authored, awaiting execution. Phase 0 plan lives here. | Move to `completed/` when done |\r\n| `session-plans/completed/` | Executed plans; archived for reference + retrospective input. | Append |\r\n| `quality-reports/{deterministic,probabilistic,drift-reports}/` | Tier-1/2/3 gate outputs (CLAUDE.md § Quality Gates). | Per-run files |\r\n| `ubiquitous-language/` | DDD glossary + domain-mapping + drift-log. Stockforge stock-domain vocabulary. | Append; canonical via `/drill-me` |\r\n| `calibration/` | Empirical hit-rate data per signal type. Confidence claims MUST trace here (CLAUDE.md hard rule). | Append per thesis post-mortem |\r\n| `research/` | Research notes from `research-scanner` subagent dispatches (e.g., reference-repo studies). | Append |\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Contract Rules (BINDING)\r\n\r\n1. **Constitution is immutable absent explicit human approval.** `Edit/Write` to `agent-workspace/constitution/**` is in `.claude/settings.json` deny list. Track 7 writes constitution drafts to `proposals/`; user explicit approve moves them.\r\n\r\n2. **`memory/decisions/` is append-mostly + supersession-status.** Don't delete decisions; mark `status: superseded-by-D-NNN` to revoke. Sequential numbering (`001`, `002`, ...) — don't reuse numbers.\r\n\r\n3. **`current-execution.md` is the routing source-of-truth.** No skill, agent, or command may hardcode phase paths or session paths from memory; resolve via this file. Stale paths in CLAUDE.md or skills = anti-pattern.\r\n\r\n4. **Never edit `obsidian-vault/raw/`.** Immutable. Vault writes only to `wiki/`. (Established in stockforge CLAUDE.md.)\r\n\r\n5. **Provenance is mandatory.** Every decision file references its source (human prompt / spec clause / drift detection / agent inference). Every thesis cites source + as-of date (I-S2). Every confidence claim cites historical hit rate (I-S20-equivalent).\r\n\r\n6. **Agents never `git commit` in this directory unless user explicitly requests.** Stage only.\r\n\r\n7. **`patterns-discovered/` artifacts are READ-ONLY for production code.** Patterns must be promoted to constitution / skills / hook scripts before becoming binding. (Otherwise they're informal notes, not contracts.)\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Reading Priority for Agent\r\n\r\nPer `agent-workspace/constitution/autonomous-protocol.md` (Track 7) and stockforge `CLAUDE.md` § Session Protocol:\r\n\r\n1. **`memory/current-execution.md`** — first; resolve active track\r\n2. **`memory/project.md`** — project state\r\n3. **`memory/checkpoints/latest.md`** if a recent checkpoint exists (within last 24h) — resume context\r\n4. **`memory/agent-notes.md`** — learned rules\r\n5. **`memory/mistake-log.md`** — pre-flight failure catalog\r\n6. **Last 3 files in `memory/sessions/`** — recent context\r\n7. **`session-plans/pending/<active-plan>.md`** — current plan\r\n8. **Relevant constitution files** as task demands (don't load all every session)\r\n9. **Relevant skills + agents + commands** as task demands\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Anti-Patterns to Avoid\r\n\r\n(From `memory/patterns-discovered/SYNTHESIS.md` § 6, full catalog 23 items. Highest-priority for this directory:)\r\n\r\n- **AP-1 Same-agent self-review** — never review your own implementation; dispatch fresh-context verifier\r\n- **AP-2 Self-track wind-down** — `.transcript-tokens` real-transcript is authoritative, not LLM self-track\r\n- **AP-5 Charter-coherence defer overriding user-CRITICAL** — re-read all `user_prompt/*` at every phase entry; never silently defer USER-CRITICAL\r\n- **AP-7 Performative SC ticking** — defer with explicit prerequisites > fire vacuous proposals\r\n- **AP-8 Pre-staged work causing checkpoint drift** — update `current-execution.md` immediately on task complete, not session-end\r\n- **AP-17 Identity drift** — stockforge is AI-first VN stock advisory; not generic financial framework (see `constitution/identity-scope.md` once Track 7 ships)\r\n- **AP-23 Continuous LLM-Guardian** — deterministic hooks = Guardian; LLM Guardian only at session-end aggregation\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Connection to human-workspace/\r\n\r\nThis directory is the agent's domain. Human's domain is `human-workspace/`. The two communicate through:\r\n- Human → Agent: `human-workspace/user_prompt/`, `human-workspace/decisions/`\r\n- Agent → Human: `human-workspace/notifications/`, `human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/`\r\n- Bidirectional: `human-workspace/q-and-a/answered/` — agent writes pending; either human or agent (per Auto-mv rule below) moves resolved bundles to answered/\r\n- Audit trail: this directory's `memory/decisions/` references `human-workspace/` source files via path pointers\r\n\r\n**Auto-mv rule (HH-E.2 — D-031 ratification, 2026-05-05)**: Agent MAY mv a bundle from `q-and-a/pending/` to `q-and-a/answered/` IFF ALL of the following hold:\r\n\r\n1. **Frontmatter signal**: bundle frontmatter `status:` field value starts with one of: `answered-`, `closed-`, `resolved-`. Examples already in repo: `answered-via-chat`, `answered-via-AskUserQuestion`, `answered-2026-05-04-via-chat`. Detection is deterministic (head -20 of file + grep `^status:`).\r\n2. **No human-veto signal**: bundle frontmatter has NO `wait_until:` ISO-8601 timestamp greater than current epoch — if present, agent MUST defer mv until that timestamp passes. Allows human to override auto-mv per-bundle without contract amendment.\r\n3. **No global pause**: file `human-workspace/q-and-a/.auto-mv-paused` does NOT exist — global kill switch for the auto-mv mechanism (single empty file presence pauses all auto-mv).\r\n4. **Hook validation**: the mv is performed by `scripts/hooks/qa-pending-auto-mover.sh` (Stop hook). Direct manual `mv` invocation by agent (e.g. via Bash tool) is STILL forbidden — only the validated hook path is authorized.\r\n\r\nAgent never writes to `human-workspace/` outside the designated `q-and-a/pending/` write channel + the auto-mv rule above + `notifications/` write channel (existing).\r\n","contentDiffersFromDisk":false},"displayPath":"agent-workspace\\CLAUDE.md"},"type":"attachment","uuid":"22e7d726-4737-416f-9c04-d6c1c06abc4d","timestamp":"2026-05-14T10:54:10.796Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"efc2e2f4-4622-42c4-be6b-a34fbc9cd3d4","version":"2.1.138","gitBranch":"main"}

Mid-Flight-Files Decision\n\n**Four violation-bearing hooks are working-tree-modified and uncommitted**:\n`escalation-engine.sh`, `severity-classifier.sh`, `autonomous-block-enforcer.sh`,\n`adr-empirical-close-verify-spot-check.sh` — carrying **~5 of the 33 violations**\n(escalation-engine L-S43b-9 + L-S48d-1; severity-classifier L-S48d-1;\nautonomous-block-enforcer L-S43b-9; adr-empirical-close-verify-spot-check L-S48d-1).\nThey are dirty from S317 (block/unblock rebuild — no session log) + 2 fully\nunattributed changes (no session log, not in any deliverable summary — checkpoint\nPRIORITY 2).\n\n**DECISION: DEFER the 4 dirty hooks to a post-commit-boundary batch (Batch E).**\n\nRationale:\n1. **Tangling risk** — editing a hook that already has uncommitted S317/unattributed\n   work means the eventual `git commit` cannot cleanly separate \"S317 block rebuild\"\n   / \"the 2 unattributed changes\" / \"S319 lint fix\". The checkpoint's PRIORITY 2 is\n   *explicitly* asking the user to create a commit boundary so S317/S318 are\n   separable. S319 mixing a third concern in deepens that exact problem.\n2. **The agent cannot commit** (CLAUDE.md hard rule) — so S319 cannot itself create\n   the boundary. It can only avoid making the tangle worse.\n3. **Provenance gap** — the 2 unattributed changes have *no session log*. Editing\n   those files before someone establishes what those changes are = editing on top of\n   an unaudited diff. P3 (surgical changes) demands knowing the baseline.\n4. **Low cost of deferral** — only ~5 of 33 violations are affected; the other ~28\n   are in clean files and can be fixed immediately with zero tangling.\n\n**Sequencing**: Batches A-D (clean files, ~28 violations) run first and are\nstandalone-committable. Batch E (the 4 dirty hooks, ~5 violations) is gated on a\n**human commit boundary** — the implementing session, at the start of Batch E, must\neither (a) confirm via `git status` that the 4 files are now clean (user committed\nS317 + investigated the 2 unattributed), or (b) if still dirty, STOP and emit a\nnotification asking the user to commit the boundary, then leave Batch E for a later\nsession. Do NOT fix-anyway on a dirty file.\n\nThis also feeds checkpoint PRIORITY 2 cleanly: \"fix the clean ones now, the dirty\nones become trivially fixable once you commit.\"\n\n## Real-vs-False-Positive Triage — L-S11-1 (Check 1)\n\nCheck 1 flags `python3?|jq|yq|pip|pip3|npm|pnpm` as a command token in a non-comment\nline. **`node` is NOT in the Check 1 banned set** — node-based JSON parsing is not a\nportability violation per this lint, so node-using hooks are not in scope.\n\nThe doctrine (L-S117-1 / L-S255-2 — \"calibrate the Guardian, don't mass-fix source\"):\nwhen a hook *legitimately* needs the tool and degrades gracefully without it, the fix\nis a lint-side skip-marker or detector refinement, NOT a bash rewrite. The\nimplementing session MUST classify each of the 10 L-S11-1 hits as REAL / FALSE-POSITIVE\n/ AMBIGUOUS by reading the actual invocation:\n\n| Hook | Architect's read (from file inspection) | Likely verdict |\n|---|---|---|\n| `attach-portability-smoke.sh` | `python -c \"import yaml...\"` — **hard dependency**, no fallback; `exit 2` FATAL if python assertion harness fails. Heavy YAML parse. | **REAL** — rewrite to bash/POSIX, OR add a `# PHASE-1+` guard if it is genuinely a Phase-1 tool. Highest-effort fix in the plan. |\n| `harness-health-self-scan.sh` | `python3` at line 72 is ONLY a fallback for `date -d` math (`date -d ... \\|\\| python3 ...`). Graceful. | **FALSE-POSITIVE** — calibrate Check 1 to skip a `python3` that is the alt-branch of a `\\|\\|` whose primary is a portable command. |\n| `autonomous-stop-watchdog.sh` | `jq` at line 32 has an explicit bash-regex fallback (`if command -v jq ...; else BASH_REMATCH ...`). Documented \"jq preferred; bash regex fallback for Windows-without-jq\". | **FALSE-POSITIVE** — `command -v jq` guarded with a complete fallback path. |\n| `redact-secrets.sh` | `python3` is the *primary* path (unicode-safe regex) with `node` 2nd and `sed` 3rd fallback. Degrades but sed branch is \"incomplete; only catches simplest patterns\". | **AMBIGUOUS** — graceful-degradation chain exists, but python3 is primary not fallback. Recommend skip-marker + a comment that the sed fallback is the Phase-0 floor. Confirm in-session. |\n| `firing-test-spawn-context-lint.sh` | inspect in-session | TBD |\n| `post-dev-dispatch-attestation-check.sh` | inspect in-session | TBD |\n| `qa-pending-stale-mover.sh` | inspect in-session | TBD |\n| `session-export-raw.sh` | inspect in-session — M-S13-pre-1 history (head -1 bug); likely real python | TBD |\n| `subagent-stop-logger.sh` | inspect in-session | TBD |\n| `vendor-api-probe.sh` | inspect in-session — a vendor-API probe almost certainly *needs* the HTTP/JSON tool legitimately | likely **FALSE-POSITIVE** or **REAL-but-Phase-1** |\n\n**Lint-calibration mechanism** (preferred over per-hook skip-markers for a project-wide\nrule, per L-S255-2): the cleanest fix for the graceful-fallback false-positives is to\nteach Check 1 to recognise the `<portable-cmd> || <banned-cmd>` and\n`if command -v <banned>; then ... else <portable-fallback> ...` shapes. If that proves\ntoo broad, fall back to a per-line `# bash-hook-lint:allow L-S11-1 <reason>` skip-marker\nthat Check 1 honours (the lint must be extended to read such markers — currently it does\nnot). EITHER mechanism requires editing `bash-hook-lint.sh` itself + a companion\nfiring-test TC proving the skip works AND that a genuine violation still fires.\n\n## Real-vs-False-Positive Triage — L-S53-2 (Check 8)\n\n**L-S53-2 also needs triage** — it is not a pure \"anchor everything\" class:\n\n- `promotion-cycle-trigger.sh:50` — **DOCUMENTED FALSE-POSITIVE**. Lines 38-46 are an\n  explicit ratify-via-comment block (per L-S55-1 recipe): the grep targets a\n  `basename` filename token (`promote-rule-S52.md`) where `S<N>` is mid-string, so\n  `^S` would never match. The comment ratifies it but does NOT silence the lint.\n- `autonomous-stop-watchdog.sh:68-77` — **DOCUMENTED FALSE-POSITIVE**. The comment\n  block explicitly says Check 8's `^` advice is WRONG here: the grep targets\n  transcript-tail narration embedded mid-JSON-line, and a P6 firing-test case\n  empirically proves anchoring would regress the detector.\n- `session-start-bootstrap.sh`, `stale-prompt-detector.sh`, `sync-grilling-call.sh` —\n  inspect in-session; some may be genuine unanchored header-greps that SHOULD get `^`.\n\nBecause `bash-hook-lint.sh` Check 8 only skips *comment lines*, a ratify-via-comment on\nthe line above a real grep does nothing. For the 2 confirmed false-positives, the fix\nis the same lint-calibration mechanism as L-S11-1: extend Check 8 to honour an\nexplicit `# bash-hook-lint:allow L-S53-2 <reason>` skip-marker on the grep line, OR\nrefine Check 8's heuristic to recognise `basename`-token and transcript-tail contexts.\nFor genuine hits, add the `^` anchor (cheap, safe).\n\n## Batch / Sequencing Strategy\n\n**RECOMMENDATION: batch BY CLASS, not by file.** Rationale:\n\n1. **Single recipe per batch** — each class has ONE documented fix recipe. A\n   by-class batch lets the dev internalise one transformation and apply it 5-10×;\n   a by-file batch context-switches between 2-3 unrelated recipes per file.\n2. **Monotonic, legible progress** — \"L-S108-1: 6 → 0\" is a clean DoD checkpoint.\n3. **The two multi-class files** (`harness-health-self-scan.sh`,\n   `escalation-engine.sh`) are touched in 2 batches each — acceptable: the edits are\n   to *different lines* for *different recipes*, and the file's firing-test is\n   re-run at each batch (catches any interaction).\n4. **Lint-calibration batches are naturally grouped** — L-S11-1 and L-S53-2 both\n   need `bash-hook-lint.sh` itself edited + `bash-hook-lint-fire-test.sh` TCs; doing\n   each class as a unit keeps the lint-self-edit coherent.\n\n**Batches** (clean files first, dirty-file batch last + gated):\n\n- **Batch A — L-S43b-9 printf-dash (2 violations)** — BUT both files\n  (`autonomous-block-enforcer.sh`, `escalation-engine.sh`) are DIRTY. **Move Batch A\n  into Batch E** (the dirty-file batch). Smallest class; trivial recipe\n  (`printf '-...'` → `printf -- '-...'`). NOTE: in both files the *obvious*\n  `printf --` lines are already correctly sentineled — the dev must `grep -nE\n  \"printf[[:space:]]+['\\\"]-\"` and find the genuine un-sentineled line; do not assume\n  it is the first printf-dash you see.\n- **Batch B — L-S108-1 session-id-fallback (6 violations, 5 files, all CLEAN)** —\n  recipe: replace `${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID:-WORD}` + `$VAR` marker filename with a date\n  hour-bucket marker (`BUCKET=\"$(date +%Y%m%d-%H)\"`) + a stale-bucket cleanup loop.\n  `idle-escape-detector.sh` is the reference implementation — it ALREADY does the\n  hour-bucket pattern correctly (lines 36-38, 54-61); the Check 6b hit on it is\n  because it ALSO still has a `${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID:-unknown}` assignment elsewhere\n  (cache filename, line 25/44) that trips the `HAS_FALLBACK` half of the detector.\n  Verify whether each hit is a real lockout risk or the detector co-triggering on a\n  benign cache-file SID — fix the real ones, and if a hit is benign, it goes through\n  L-S11-1-style lint calibration.\n- **Batch C — L-S48d-1 pipefail-bare-grep (5 violations; 2 CLEAN, 3 DIRTY)** — CLEAN\n  subset: `bootstrap-summary-renderer.sh`, `harness-health-self-scan.sh`. DIRTY\n  subset: `adr-empirical-close-verify-spot-check.sh`, `escalation-engine.sh`,\n  `severity-classifier.sh` → those 3 move to Batch E. Recipe: wrap each unguarded\n  grep with `|| true`, or convert to `if grep ...; then` form. CAUTION: Check 7's\n  awk detector has known gaps — `adr-empirical-close-verify-spot-check.sh:86-89`\n  appears to already guard with `|| true` inside a `{ }` brace+timeout structure;\n  `severity-classifier.sh:143-153` already wraps the pipeline in `( ... ) || true`.\n  These may be **detector false-positives** — the dev must read each flagged file\n  and decide: real unguarded grep (fix the grep) vs. Check 7 awk gap (refine Check 7\n  + add a firing-test TC). Do NOT add a redundant `|| true` to an already-guarded\n  pipeline just to silence the lint.\n- **Batch D — L-S80-2 grep-c-capture-trap (7 violations; mostly CLEAN)** — recipe:\n  replace `VAR=$(grep -c ... || echo N)` with `if grep -qE ...; then VAR=1; else\n  VAR=0; fi`. CAUTION on two files:\n    - `daily-backup.sh:88` — the trap is `VERIFY_HITS=$(tar -tzf ... | grep -cE ... || echo 0)`\n      i.e. grep -c on a *pipeline*, not a standalone file. The simple `if grep -qE`\n      recipe must be adapted: `if tar -tzf \"$ARCHIVE\" 2>/dev/null | grep -qE '...';\n      then VERIFY_HITS=1; else VERIFY_HITS=0; fi`. `daily-backup.sh` is committed R3\n      mass-deletion-prevention code — keep the fix surgical (P3) and re-run its\n      firing-test (`daily-backup-fire-test.sh`).\n    - `idle-escape-detector.sh:76` — the `grep -c ... || echo 0` sits AFTER a `set +o\n      pipefail` (line 69), so the multi-line `\"0\\nN\"` risk is largely neutralised.\n      Still apply the if/then/fi recipe for correctness + to clear the lint, but this\n      is low-urgency.\n- **Batch L (lint-calibration) — L-S11-1 (10) + L-S53-2 (5)** — this is the\n  triage-heavy batch. Split into two sub-steps:\n    - **L.1** — triage all 10 L-S11-1 + all 5 L-S53-2 hits (REAL / FALSE-POSITIVE /\n      AMBIGUOUS) per § Triage sections; write the verdict table into the session log.\n    - **L.2** — for REAL hits: rewrite to bash/POSIX (L-S11-1) or add `^` anchor\n      (L-S53-2). For FALSE-POSITIVE hits: extend `bash-hook-lint.sh` Check 1 / Check 8\n      (skip-marker support or heuristic refinement) + add `bash-hook-lint-fire-test.sh`\n      TCs proving (a) the false-positive no longer fires AND (b) a genuine violation\n      still fires. `bash-hook-lint.sh` is itself a hook with a companion firing-test —\n      Principle 11 applies to the lint's own edit.\n- **Batch E — dirty-file batch (gated on commit boundary)** — `escalation-engine.sh`\n  (L-S43b-9 + L-S48d-1), `severity-classifier.sh` (L-S48d-1),\n  `autonomous-block-enforcer.sh` (L-S43b-9), `adr-empirical-close-verify-spot-check.sh`\n  (L-S48d-1). GATE: at Batch E start, `git status --short` these 4 files. If CLEAN →\n  proceed (apply Batch A + Batch C recipes to them). If still DIRTY → STOP, emit a\n  notification asking the user to commit the S317/unattributed boundary, defer Batch E\n  to a later session. The ~5 violations here are the only ones that may not close in\n  S319.\n\n**Suggested batch order within a session**: B → D → C(clean subset) → L → E.\n(B and D are pure-recipe and high-count — fast wins, monotonic count drop. C-clean\nis small. L is the slow triage batch. E is gated and may not run.)\n\n## Session Sizing\n\n33 violations across ~25 files + lint-self-calibration + per-batch firing-test\nre-runs + a full `run-all.sh` regression at each batch boundary does NOT fit one\nFOCUSED_IMPL envelope. **Proposed split: 2 FOCUSED_IMPL sub-sessions + 1 optional\nVERIFY.**\n\n- **S319a (FOCUSED_IMPL, ~100-120K)** — STEP 0 pre-flight + Batch B (L-S108-1, 6) +\n  Batch D (L-S80-2, 7) + Batch C-clean-subset (L-S48d-1 ×2). ~15 violations closed.\n  Pure-recipe work, low triage load. DoD: those classes' counts hit 0/0 for the\n  clean files; `run-all.sh` still 103/103.\n- **S319b (FOCUSED_IMPL, ~120-140K)** — Batch L (L-S11-1 ×10 + L-S53-2 ×5) — the\n  triage-heavy batch incl. editing `bash-hook-lint.sh` itself + firing-test TC\n  authoring + the `attach-portability-smoke.sh` python→bash rewrite (the single\n  largest fix). ~13 violations closed (some via real fix, some via ratified lint\n  calibration). DoD: L-S11-1 + L-S53-2 either 0 or 0-plus-documented-FP; the lint's\n  own firing-test green.\n- **Batch E** — slot into S319b *if* the commit boundary exists by then; otherwise\n  its own short follow-up session S319c after the user commits. ~5 violations.\n- **S319-verify (VERIFY, ~30-50K, optional but recommended)** — fresh-context\n  sandwich-verifier: re-run the lint, confirm count, adversarially probe that no\n  \"fix\" is a ghost-green (e.g. a redundant `|| true` slapped on an already-guarded\n  grep, or a skip-marker hiding a real violation). Per AP-1, the implementing dev\n  must NOT self-verify the final count.\n\n**Total estimate: 2 IMPL sessions (~220-260K combined) + 1 optional VERIFY (~40K),\nwith Batch E possibly spilling to a 3rd short session if the commit boundary lags.**\n\n## Per-Batch Definition of Done\n\nEvery batch, without exception:\n\n1. ✅ **Lint count drops monotonically** — re-run\n   `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=\"$(pwd)\" bash scripts/hooks/bash-hook-lint.sh </dev/null` and\n   read `human-workspace/notifications/bash-hook-lint-warn.md`. The total MUST be\n   strictly lower than at batch start (or equal, only if the batch was pure\n   lint-calibration that converted N hard-violations into N documented-false-positives\n   — in which case the session log must say so explicitly with the N count).\n2. ✅ **Firing-test regression holds** — `bash scripts/hooks/firing-tests/run-all.sh`\n   ≥ 103/103. If a violation fix required a companion firing-test update (Principle\n   11), that update lands IN the same batch and the suite count may rise but never\n   fall.\n3. ✅ **`bash -n` clean** on every edited hook.\n4. ✅ **Each edited hook's own firing-test** runs green individually (not just the\n   aggregate) — e.g. after editing `daily-backup.sh`, run\n   `bash scripts/hooks/firing-tests/daily-backup-fire-test.sh` directly.\n5. ✅ **No ghost-green** — a \"fix\" that merely silences the lint without addressing\n   the root cause (redundant `|| true` on already-guarded grep; skip-marker on a real\n   violation) is FORBIDDEN. If a hit is a detector false-positive, the fix is a\n   detector refinement + a firing-test TC proving real violations still fire — never\n   a no-op source edit.\n6. ✅ Batch is **standalone-committable** — the diff touches only the files in that\n   batch's scope (P3).\n\n**Whole-plan DoD**:\n- ✅ `bash scripts/hooks/bash-hook-lint.sh` → 0 violations, OR 0-plus-N where every\n  surviving N is a ratified false-positive with a lint-side suppression + firing-test\n  TC, documented in the session log with the N count and per-file reason.\n- ✅ `human-workspace/notifications/bash-hook-lint-warn.md` deleted (the lint\n  auto-`rm`s it when VIOLATIONS==0 — see `bash-hook-lint.sh` line 461).\n- ✅ Full firing-test regression ≥ 103/103 reproduced ≥2× (per S318 verifier rigor).\n- ✅ `bash-hook-lint.sh` itself, if edited for calibration, has updated\n  `bash-hook-lint-fire-test.sh` coverage and still passes.\n- ✅ Session logs for S319a / S319b (/ S319c) per CLAUDE.md Session Protocol.\n- ✅ `mistake-log.md` updated OR explicit \"no mistakes this session\" per session.\n- ✅ NO git commit (CLAUDE.md hard rule) — changes staged; the user owns the commit\n   boundary (this plan deliberately keeps the dirty-file batch separate to HELP that).\n\n## Risks & Gotchas\n\n1. **Risk — the ratify-via-comment trap (HIGH).** `promotion-cycle-trigger.sh` and\n   `autonomous-stop-watchdog.sh` already have inline comments ratifying their L-S53-2\n   hits, yet the lint still counts them. A dev who adds *another* comment will not\n   move the count. **Mitigation**: the only count-reducing fix for a false-positive\n   is a lint-side change (skip-marker support or heuristic refinement) — Batch L.2\n   makes this explicit.\n\n2. **Risk — Check 7 / Check 10 detector gaps cause false-positives (MEDIUM).**\n   `adr-empirical-close-verify-spot-check.sh` and `severity-classifier.sh` appear to\n   already guard their flagged greps (`{ ... || true; }` / `( ... ) || true`). {"parentUuid":"e08e4a79-8154-418b-ba15-72a4cb7a1ec7","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"nested_memory","path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\human-workspace\\CLAUDE.md","content":{"path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\human-workspace\\CLAUDE.md","type":"Project","content":"# human-workspace/ — Contract\r\n\r\n> **Audience**: agents reading anything inside `human-workspace/`.\r\n> **Established**: Decision 002 § Track 1 (Workspace Dualism Foundation).\r\n\r\n## Identity\r\n\r\n`human-workspace/` is the **human-authored authority** layer. Everything here represents **human decisions, scope, intent, and verification**. Agents READ this directory as authoritative; agents do NOT WRITE here except in one designated channel (`q-and-a/pending/` — where agents post questions for human to answer).\r\n\r\nThis separation exists because of a failure mode observed in the orch sister project (orch `decisions/040`, post-mortem CF-DOGFOOD-2): when human and agent share a single workspace without contract, agent silently overrides human-CRITICAL items via technical-defer logic. The user explicitly raised this concern in `human-workspace/user_prompt/20260429_02_init.txt` §1.1.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Subdirectories\r\n\r\n| Path | Purpose | Who writes |\r\n|---|---|---|\r\n| `user_prompt/` | Human's mid-flight scope/idea drops. Naming: `YYYYMMDD_NN_<slug>.txt`. Files are immutable post-creation (audit trail). | **Human only**. Agent: read-only. |\r\n| `decisions/` | Human's strategic decisions (e.g., scope-lock, charter-revision-trigger, peer-share authorization). Format: `D-H-<NNN>-<slug>.md`. | **Human only**. Agent: read-only. |\r\n| `q-and-a/pending/` | **The ONE channel where agent writes inside human-workspace**. Agent drops Q&A bundles per Grill Maximization doctrine; human responds inline or moves to `answered/`. | **Both** (agent writes new bundles; human writes answers). |\r\n| `q-and-a/answered/` | Q&A bundles human has answered (with answers inline). Agent reads answers and acts. Archive forever; provenance trail. | **Human moves** (drag from `pending/`); agent reads. |\r\n| `q-and-a/stale/` | Pending bundles that exceeded their `expected_answer_by` (default 24h, urgent 4h). Auto-moved by SessionStart hook (Track 5). | **Hook moves**; both read. |\r\n| `notifications/` | Agent push to human — summaries, alerts, milestones. Format: `N-<TS>-<level>-<slug>.md`. Levels: INFO / SUMMARY / ALERT. | **Agent writes**; human reads. |\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Contract Rules (BINDING)\r\n\r\n1. **Agent NEVER writes to `user_prompt/` or `decisions/`.** Permission deny. If something feels like a human decision but the human hasn't written it, dispatch a Q&A bundle into `q-and-a/pending/` instead.\r\n\r\n2. **`user_prompt/` files are immutable post-creation.** Agent never deletes, renames, or edits these files. They are the audit trail of human interventions.\r\n\r\n3. **Q&A bundle format** (per Track 4 spec): YAML frontmatter (`id`, `topic`, `opened_at`, `expected_answer_by`, `priority`, `related_decisions`, `status`) + question body + answer-fill section. Each bundle = up to 25 questions per Grill Maximization doctrine; split if more.\r\n\r\n4. **Agent does not move files between `q-and-a/{pending,answered,stale}/`** — that's human's role (or hook's, in case of stale). Agent only WRITES new pending bundles and READS answers.\r\n\r\n5. **Notifications are read-only for human.** Human shouldn't edit `notifications/*` files; if disagreement with notification content, drop a `user_prompt/` instead. Notifications are the agent's account of events.\r\n\r\n6. **Provenance pointers**: every `agent-workspace/memory/decisions/D-<NNN>` should reference its source `human-workspace/user_prompt/<file>` or `human-workspace/decisions/D-H-<NNN>` if the agent's decision derives from human input.\r\n\r\n7. **No multi-tenancy in this directory.** Per identity-scope.md (Track 7), stockforge is single-tenant Phase 0-5; if peer share happens it's via git-fork, each peer has their own `human-workspace/` per fork.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Reading Priority for Agent\r\n\r\nWhen loading session context (per `agent-workspace/constitution/autonomous-protocol.md` Track 7):\r\n\r\n1. **All `user_prompt/*.txt`** — every prompt, not just most recent. Per orch lesson (decision-040 USER-CRITICAL tier): never silently defer human-CRITICAL items.\r\n2. **All `decisions/*.md`** — human's strategic decisions are above charter principles in priority; charter is below human (charter was authored by human in the first place).\r\n3. **Latest `q-and-a/answered/*`** — recent answers update agent's understanding.\r\n4. **Open `q-and-a/pending/*`** — flag if waiting on human answers.\r\n5. **Recent `notifications/*`** (last 7 days) — for situational awareness.\r\n\r\n---\r\n\r\n## Agent Self-Check\r\n\r\nBefore writing to `human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/`, ask:\r\n- Is this question genuinely something the human must decide? (Charter principle / Charter-affecting / SCOPE-affecting / above ARCH-tier confidence threshold)\r\n- Have I already grilled this in a recent bundle? (Don't ask twice; don't pollute pending/)\r\n- Am I bundling per Grill Maximization (target 15-20 questions, max 25)? Or splintering across many small bundles?\r\n\r\nIf the answer to any is \"I'm not sure\" — DON'T write the bundle. Either answer it yourself with charter-principle reasoning + log decision, or wait until ambiguity clears.\r\n","contentDiffersFromDisk":false},"displayPath":"human-workspace\\CLAUDE.md"},"type":"attachment","uuid":"2f19a536-1d6b-431f-a079-7c4558fef9cd","timestamp":"2026-05-14T11:00:40.747Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"efc2e2f4-4622-42c4-be6b-a34fbc9cd3d4","version":"2.1.138","gitBranch":"main"}
